reasons.reader_question: The guest, Ila going still at 'sixty' and her hand on the hidden letter give a sharp, predictable-but-uncertain question. The letter thread is implied, not named.
reasons.change: Kunal moves from guarded to exposed. He gives the lakes and admits the steering, and the crown's sheet now holds both the name and his evasion.
reasons.romance_movement: This is a new reason: his first costed true disclosure, met by her open, exact record of his evasion. 'I write what's true, even when it's you' lands the beat.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Chemistry shows in responsive action: 'Holes with rules round them' and his surprised laugh, her asking before writing, his pink fingertips checked after 'Yes'.
reasons.character_logic: Kunal walks toward a way his family never walks in winter and no one remarks on it. The Dhanu trade-off is well reasoned and owned.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: The left fork costs Dhanu's party a day alone against Raghu's glass. Kunal weighs it and names his shame, which ties to the later loss.
reasons.prose: The prose is clean and concrete, with no banned phrases. The cliff-rule realisation paragraph is muddled, there are 'Of course she...' echoes, and Kunal's 'very' tic repeats from ch9.
reasons.continuity: Ch9 and F687 say a toppled keeper cairn darkens the line beyond it. Here the line returns in cloud with no cause given.

fixes: At "They broke the door. They didn't break the road." (Convenient magic; this contradicts ch9 and F687). Keep the stretch past the door dark. Have the thread show only from the next intact cairn up the shoulder, glowing in the cloud. Kunal crosses the dark gap by memory and route-song, and says plainly that only the door's stretch forgot itself.

At "No one of our blood walks it between first snow and thaw" (Irrational behaviour; Kunal is walking it now). Have Ila ask, 'And you're taking me toward it in winter.' Kunal answers truly that he is breaking the rule, and why. Change 'And he made the rule' so it doesn't clash with Pritam's ch17 sharing rule (F526). Move the 'my father said' line before Kunal was nine.

At "By their own cliff rule, a name said once" (muddled interiority; he gave the name on purpose, so the rule doesn't apply). Replace it with two plain sentences: he meant it, so the name is hers to write, and her hand went to her coat. Cut one of the two 'Of course she...' lines.
reader_question: Who was the guest Prince Udai led up in winter sixty years ago and came down without, and now that Kunal has named the Glass Lakes, will Ila open the queen's letter?
new_facts_assessment: F690 holds up: tracks a day or two old plus the half-day detour gives a full day. F691 is consistent with F473 and F685, and it is needed because it creates the cost of the left fork and seeds Dhanu's fate. Both facts are sound. The unlisted additions, the winter-walking rule and 'Udai made the rule', sit uneasily with F526 (ch17: Pritam tells the story and makes a no-sharing rule) and need reconciling.
